title: Comunicado 2025-03-20
summary: The SARB MPC held the repo rate at 7.50% by a 4-2 vote, with two members favouring a further 25bp cut, and framed the pause as a 'cautious policy approach' because extreme global uncertainty (tariffs, shifting geopolitics, rates high for longer abroad) and domestic risks threaten the recent compression of the country risk premium and bond yields. Versus the January statement, the split flips sides: January cut 25bp with two members wanting to hold, while March holds with two members wanting to cut. The macro case for easing actually strengthened, with the headline inflation forecast lowered (fuel and electricity tariffs more than offsetting the VAT increase), inflation 'contained' in the bottom half of the range and growth revised down with risks now to the downside rather than balanced; but the inflation risk balance stays tilted up in the medium term. The QPM path still points to rates stabilising near a neutral 7.25%, implying one more cut eventually, with decisions meeting by meeting: a hold with the door open to easing.

key_quotes.quote: Four members preferred this action, while two favoured a cut of 25 basis points.
key_quotes.context: Hold at 7.5% with a dovish minority of two wanting to keep cutting; in January the minority of two wanted to hold

key_quotes.quote: This calls for a cautious policy approach.
key_quotes.context: Pause justified by global instability and domestic uncertainties that put the lower risk premium and bond yields at risk

key_quotes.quote: As before, the forecast sees rates stabilising at a neutral level of about 7.25%.
key_quotes.context: QPM path implies one more cut from 7.5% to neutral; current stance only mildly restrictive

key_quotes.quote: We assess that the risks to growth are to the downside.
key_quotes.context: Growth risk balance moves from balanced (January) to downside, with 2025 growth revised to 1.7%
